source.title: How does topology influence gradient propagation and model performance of deep networks with DenseNet-type skip connections?
source.authors: K. Bhardwaj; Gui-Hong Li; R. Marculescu

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary information are present; some proceedings text is interleaved and garbled, but the relevant training-convergence discussion is readable.
record.tranche_reason: Compares training convergence across DenseNet-type MLPs with different depths, parameter counts, and NN-Mass, a related test of how network structure affects gradient-trained convergence.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR-10/100 experiments report test accuracy, not training classification error. Training-convergence results are for MNIST MLPs and are shown only in Figure 4; the text describes relative convergence but gives no final training-error values.
record.test_reason: The study tests how skip-connection topology predicts gradient properties, training convergence and test accuracy. Its MNIST convergence comparisons vary topology rather than initialization, normalization or identity residual shortcuts. Its CIFAR/ImageNet results measure test accuracy, so they do not establish the training-error effects in V1 or V3. None of V1–V6 is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that models with similar width and NN-Mass exhibit similar layerwise gradient properties and training convergence despite different depths and parameter counts. They also report that NN-Mass identifies architectures with similar test accuracy and enables direct design of compressed models.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies randomly connected DenseNet-type architectures and NN-Mass; it does not reproduce the listed training-error studies or compare their recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported convergence comparison varies depth, parameter count, and NN-Mass; the text reports faster convergence for the higher-NN-Mass model in the described group.

fits_no_version.finding: MNIST ELU MLPs of width eight with similar NN-Mass have nearly coincident training-convergence curves despite different depths and parameter counts; higher-NN-Mass Z converges faster than Y.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the tested DenseNet-type MNIST MLPs, skip-connection topology summarized by NN-Mass predicts relative training convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: Initial mean layerwise Jacobian singular values correlate more strongly with NN-Mass than parameter count; CNN comparisons principally report test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: NN-Mass predicts initial layerwise gradient proxies and test performance across the tested architectures.

record.problems: The training-convergence comparisons are shown only as plots, without stated final training-error values; the text gives qualitative comparisons. The reported convergence comparison is on MNIST MLPs, not the CIFAR convolutional settings in V1.
record.rows_left_out: CIFAR-10/100 results report test accuracy rather than training classification error, so they were not extracted as rows for these versions. Figure 4(b,c) is described as showing similar observations for additional model groups, but the supplied text does not state their individual model details or outcomes sufficiently to create separate rows.

untested.parts: Near-zero CIFAR-10/100 training classification error under gradient training, including corrupted/random labels and model-size or regularization qualifications.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their reduction through student overwidth.
Depth-related training-error degradation in plain batch-normalized CNNs, its prevention by identity residual shortcuts, and the special-initialization exceptions.
Effects of activation-matched initialization on learning speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal-versus-Gaussian comparisons.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, transient loss growth and recovery, sharpness trajectories and divergence.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including the Fixup alternative.

record.verdict_notes: The statement that shortcut-free models degrade with depth concerns test-accuracy clusters and an explanation involving diminishing gradients; it does not report the training-error comparison required by V3. Initialization is held comparable rather than experimentally contrasted. Batch normalization is used in the CNNs without an ablation.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/100 training classification error, corrupted or random labels, and whether the tested recipes reach near-zero training error.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus identity-residual networks and the effects of depth on training error.
Comparisons of initialization schemes and their effects on training speed or trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss recovery, sharpness, and divergence.
A comparison of otherwise matched networks with and without batch normalization.

rows.subject: Model X

rows.measure: Training accuracy over epochs; text says its convergence nearly coincides with Model Y.
rows.note: Text describes relative convergence, but supplies no final training accuracy or classification error.
rows.check: The qualitative result is readable: X and Y have nearly coincident convergence curves. It measures a topology comparison outside the claim versions; missing final training-error numbers are not the main reason it cannot establish a version.

rows.subject: Model Y
rows.operation_detail: Training convergence on MNIST, plotted as training accuracy over epochs.

rows.note: Text describes relative convergence, but supplies no final training accuracy or classification error.
rows.check: The qualitative result is readable: Y and X have nearly coincident convergence curves. Neither their different depths nor their concatenation shortcuts establish the plain-versus-identity-residual training-error comparison in V3.

rows.subject: Model Z
rows.operation_detail: Training convergence on MNIST, plotted as training accuracy over epochs.

conditions.value: Model Y has 32 layers and nearly the same parameter count

rows.measure: Training accuracy over epochs; text says convergence is significantly faster than Model Y.
rows.note: Text attributes faster convergence to higher NN-Mass, but supplies no final training accuracy or classification error.
rows.check: The text explicitly reports faster convergence for Z than Y, but attributes it to higher NN-Mass. Their parameter counts are approximately matched, not identical: 8.3K versus 9.0K. This does not test any listed version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
